idea_name: Crop Stress Early Warning That Fires Before NDVI Moves
one_sentence_pitch: For EU arable farmers and CAP/insurance monitoring bodies who today only learn a field is stressed once NDVI has already dropped (i.e. after yield is lost), a self-supervised anomaly detector fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical time series learns each parcel's normal phenological trajectory and flags divergence days before the NDVI-threshold rule fires, with the technical core being a fused-modality temporal autoencoder scored against a measured lead-time-in-days metric rather than a classification accuracy number.
problem_statement: The dominant operational practice for crop stress monitoring, used by farmers, agronomists, and index-insurance schemes, is to watch NDVI (or similar optical vegetation indices) and raise an alert when it drops below a threshold or deviates from its historical seasonal norm (as in the EC JRC ASAP/MARS system and near-real-time MODIS NDVI anomaly monitoring). This is fundamentally a lagging indicator: canopy greenness only changes after physiological damage (cell/tissue-level water or nitrogen deficit, early disease) has already occurred, so by the time the NDVI-threshold rule fires, some yield loss is already locked in. Farmers and insurers have no widely deployed method that is dated, alerts before the optical signal moves, and is validated on how many days of lead time it actually buys, as opposed to how accurately it classifies stress after the fact.
proposed_technical_approach: A self-supervised anomaly detector operating on joint Sentinel-1 (VV/VH backscatter) and Sentinel-2 (NDVI/NDRE/GNDVI-derived optical time series) per-parcel time series. Architecture: a 3D convolutional or ConvLSTM-based autoencoder (following the general recipe of STS-NET's 3D-CAE but extended to two input streams) that learns to reconstruct/predict each parcel's expected multi-band trajectory conditioned on its own phenological history and crop-type/growth-stage context; the reconstruction error (or a learned normality score) at each new acquisition is the anomaly signal. Training objective: self-supervised reconstruction or next-step prediction loss over historical, presumed-normal seasons only (no stress labels needed for training). Inference/output: for each parcel and each new Sentinel-1/2 acquisition, a dated anomaly score; an alert fires the first time the score crosses a threshold calibrated on a held-out normal-season set. Evaluation: lead-time-in-days = date(NDVI-threshold-rule alert) minus date(fused-model alert), computed per parcel, compared against a named NDVI-only anomaly baseline reproducing the ASAP/Meroni et al. near-real-time NDVI anomaly logic. A SAR-only vs. optical-only vs. fused ablation isolates whether the SAR channel is actually contributing lead time (this ablation is a mandatory early check, see risks).

total_dataset_gb: Approximately 15-30 GB for a minimum viable pilot (one or two EU regions, one growing season, Sentinel-1+2 time series clipped to a modest AOI plus AI4Boundaries parcel geometries) - well under the ~200GB practical H5 ceiling.
labels_and_ground_truth: The model itself is trained self-supervised (reconstruction/prediction error against each parcel's own historical normal trajectory) and needs no stress labels for training. The hard dependency is on the EVALUATION side: measuring 'lead time' credibly requires a dated, independent record of when real crop stress actually began. A systematic search (arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, WebSearch) did not surface a public, parcel-level, dated crop-stress-onset dataset for either the EU or Southeast Asia at the needed granularity - STS-NET's own BSPT ground-truth dataset is private and covers one 2.5-acre plot in India. The workable substitute is a self-referential proxy: define the comparison event as the date the NDVI-threshold rule itself would have fired (replicating the ASAP/Meroni logic), and measure the fused model's lead time relative to that, rather than to an independent physiological ground truth. This is defensible as a direct head-to-head against the named baseline practice, but it does not, by itself, prove the alert corresponds to real agronomic stress - a small set of field-verified events (via a local agronomist contact or a well-documented historical drought/flood year) is needed to sanity-check that the earlier alerts are not simply noise-driven false positives. [uncertain: whether any usable dated ground-truth stress record exists beyond this self-referential proxy]

evaluation_protocol: Primary metric: lead-time-in-days, defined per flagged parcel as date(NDVI-threshold-rule alert, replicating Meroni/ASAP logic) minus date(fused SAR+optical anomaly-score threshold crossing), reported as a distribution (median, IQR) over a held-out set of parcels and growing seasons. Secondary metrics: false-alert rate per parcel-season (alerts with no corresponding NDVI-threshold crossing within a following window), and a SAR-vs-optical-vs-fused ablation reporting each channel's marginal lead-time contribution. Geographic/temporal generalisation: train the self-supervised model on one region/season's parcels only, evaluate lead time on a held-out region and/or held-out season to test whether the learned 'normal phenology' transfers. Success would be a positive median lead time (multiple days) that survives the ablation, i.e. is not attributable to optical bands alone.
novelty_delta: STS-NET (arXiv:2607.18791, 2026) establishes that self-supervised crop-stress detection from satellite image time series is viable, using a 3D convolutional autoencoder over four optical vegetation indices derived from commercial PlanetScope imagery, evaluated by classification precision on sugarcane stress types. It explicitly does not use SAR and does not measure or report anything resembling lead time - its headline numbers are precision percentages, not days-early. The candidate's delta is two orthogonal, defensible changes, not a region swap: (1) a new data regime - free-tier Sentinel-1 SAR fused with Sentinel-2 optical, exploiting a physically distinct sensing channel (radar backscatter sensitive to canopy structure/water content) that the cited prior art never uses; (2) a new evaluation objective - the headline number is lead-time-in-days measured against a named, currently-deployed NDVI-anomaly practice (ASAP/Meroni), not a classification accuracy score. Neither change is present in the cited baseline, and 'applied a self-supervised detector to Sentinel data' would not by itself pass H1 without the lead-time framing, which is the actual technical claim.
prior_art_that_threatens_it: Huo, Persson & Lindberg (2021, RSE, DOI 10.1016/j.rse.2020.112240) already fused Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 to detect pre-visual forest stress (European spruce bark beetle) and found that Sentinel-1 backscatter contributed only marginally to classification accuracy beyond the red/SWIR optical bands - this is a genuine, closely analogous result that threatens the specific claim that 'SAR is the key early-signal channel' for crops; the domain differs (forest pest vs. crop water/nitrogen stress) so it is not dispositive, but it means the SAR contribution must be empirically demonstrated, not assumed. Le Page et al. (2020, RS MDPI, DOI 10.3390/rs12101621) already showed Sentinel-1 soil-moisture-derived signals can detect irrigation events at plot scale, supporting the premise that SAR senses water-status changes early, but this was not assembled into a self-supervised anomaly detector with a lead-time metric. No 2024-2026 paper was found (arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, dblp all searched) that combines self-supervised S1+S2 fusion anomaly detection with an explicit lead-time-in-days metric benchmarked against a named NDVI-threshold baseline; this specific combination appears to remain open, though the individual ingredients (fusion, self-supervision, pre-visual stress signal) are each separately precedented.
h2_generic_check: Confirmed NOT a banned pattern: not a chatbot/RAG assistant, not a dashboard/monitoring portal, not leaf-photo disease classification, explicitly NOT a plain NDVI viewer (the whole point is to beat NDVI), not tabular yield prediction from weather/soil CSVs, not a crop-type-classification benchmark rerun, not an API-wrapper mobile app. Could the one-sentence summary describe 50 other FYPs? No - most 'satellite crop monitoring' student projects report classification accuracy after the fact; committing to a measured days-of-lead-time headline metric against a named operational baseline is a specific, falsifiable technical claim that is uncommon in typical FYP framing.
user_segment: Primary: EU arable/horticultural farmers and the agronomists/advisory services and index-insurance providers that serve them, particularly where CAP monitoring (Sen4CAP/LPIS) already provides parcel-level infrastructure - e.g. a pilot region in France, the Netherlands, or another AI4Boundaries-covered country. Secondary/aspirational: Malaysian or Indonesian oil-palm/rice smallholder agronomists and estate managers, framed as a future deployment target, but this is weaker evidence-wise: Malaysia lacks the equivalent public parcel-level ground-truth infrastructure (LPIS/AI4Boundaries has no SEA equivalent found), and persistent cloud cover degrades the optical channel exactly where the fusion story matters most (see N1 tension). [uncertain: final geography choice between EU and SEA not resolved by this research pass; EU is better evidenced]
quantified_pain: Turvey & McLaurin (2012, Weather Climate and Society, DOI 10.1175/wcas-d-11-00059.1) found NDVI-based index insurance is highly location-dependent and unreliable without site-specific calibration across 60 US locations 1982-2003, directly evidencing that the current NDVI-threshold practice is a poor and lagging basis for insurance decisions. The broader remote-sensing water-stress literature (Gerhards et al. 2019 review, DOI 10.3390/rs11101240) repeatedly notes that physiological water stress precedes visible canopy/NDVI symptoms, meaning yield-relevant damage is typically already underway by the time an NDVI-threshold alert fires. [uncertain: no single hard industry figure (e.g. 'USD X million lost annually to late detection') was found in this search pass; the pain is evidenced qualitatively across multiple sources rather than by one quantified statistic]

compute_feasibility.peak_memory_gb: Estimated well under 10GB - a 3D-CAE/ConvLSTM over small spatial patches (e.g. 32x32-64x64px) per parcel time series is comparable in scale to STS-NET's reported lightweight 3D-CAE
compute_feasibility.est_training_hours_mps: Estimated 3-8 hours for a single-region pilot dataset (15-30GB) on Apple M4 Pro MPS backend
compute_feasibility.mps_compatible_ops: 3D convolutions, ConvLSTM/GRU cells, and standard autoencoder losses are all supported on PyTorch MPS; no custom CUDA kernels required
compute_feasibility.colab_kaggle_fallback_needed: Not strictly required, but available as a buffer if the fused two-sensor time series extraction proves memory-heavy during preprocessing
compute_feasibility.notes: Estimates are extrapolated from the architecture scale described in STS-NET's abstract and comparable published S1+S2 fusion models (e.g. Van Tricht et al. 2018 random-forest fusion, which is far lighter); not independently benchmarked in this research pass

cash_cost_rm: Approximately RM 0 for core data and compute (Sentinel-1/2 and AI4Boundaries are free; MPS training is on the student's own MacBook Pro). A small buffer (~RM 30-50) for optional Colab Pro compute credits if the two-sensor time-series preprocessing needs more RAM than available locally. No commercial imagery dependency - the design deliberately avoids STS-NET's own use of commercial PlanetScope imagery.
demo_artifact: A live laptop demo replaying a held-out parcel's Sentinel-1+2 time series week-by-week: the anomaly score curve is shown rising and crossing its threshold on a specific date, plotted alongside the NDVI curve which crosses its own operational threshold N days later - the panel watches the fused-model alert fire first and sees the day-count difference displayed live, with a toggle to show the SAR-only/optical-only/fused ablation on the same parcel.
build_vs_research_ratio: Approximately 70:30 engineering:research. The bulk of the effort is data-pipeline engineering: STAC/openEO querying, Sentinel-1 speckle filtering and orbit-based revisit alignment, Sentinel-2 cloud masking, per-parcel time-series extraction and temporal alignment across two sensors with different revisit cadences, plus the self-supervised model and the live demo dashboard. The research component is validating the lead-time claim, running the SAR-contribution ablation, and testing geographic generalisation.
publication_venue_fit: IGARSS (strong fit for an applied SAR+optical fusion methods paper with a novel evaluation metric) or Remote Sensing (MDPI) for a full applied-EO paper; ICLR ML4RS workshop is also plausible given the self-supervised-anomaly-detection framing and the explicit comparison against STS-NET.
key_risks: 1. Ground-truth/evaluation risk (highest): no independent, dated, parcel-level crop-stress-onset dataset was found publicly for the EU or SEA at the needed granularity; the self-referential NDVI-crossing proxy risks circularity (the model may just be detecting an earlier-triggering variant of the same optical signal rather than genuinely independent stress).

2. Method risk: Huo et al. (2021) found SAR contributed only marginally beyond optical bands in a closely analogous pre-visual stress detection setting (forest bark beetle); the core premise that 'SAR buys real lead time' for crops may not replicate and must be tested via ablation in week 1-2, not assumed.

3. Revisit-cadence and cloud-cover risk: Sentinel-1 (6-12 day) and Sentinel-2 (5-day nominal but cloud-degraded) have mismatched, geography-dependent effective revisit rates; a tropical SEA pilot site would face the worst cloud conditions exactly where the fusion argument is supposed to matter most (tension with N1).

4. Geography-choice risk: the EU gives better ground-truth infrastructure (AI4Boundaries, ASAP/MARS) but weakens the Singapore/Malaysia user-segment framing required to strongly satisfy H4; this needs an explicit, justified design decision, not an implicit default.

5. Data-reuse risk: STS-NET's own BSPT dataset and PlanetScope imagery are not reusable (private/commercial), so the student must assemble their own small field-verified event set from scratch, a real logistics constraint within an FYP timeline.
kill_criteria: Week 1: Query the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem STAC catalogue for the candidate AOI and measure the actual per-pixel cloud-free Sentinel-2 revisit rate over a full growing season; if it is so degraded (especially for a tropical SEA site) that the optical baseline itself cannot be computed reliably, abandon that geography.

Week 1-2: Attempt to source at least 5-10 dated, field-verified stress events (via a local agronomist contact, a documented historical drought/flood year, or an EU national crop-condition bulletin); if zero can be obtained, decide explicitly whether the self-referential NDVI-crossing proxy is an acceptable evaluation for the panel before investing further.

Week 2: Run the SAR-vs-optical-vs-fused ablation on any available small sample, replicating Huo et al.'s comparison; if SAR's marginal lead-time contribution over optical alone is statistically indistinguishable from zero, reframe the pitch around fusion-robustness (e.g. cloud-gap resilience) rather than SAR-driven earliness, or abandon the SAR angle.

hard_constraint_verdict.H1: PASS - genuine two-part delta (new SAR+optical data regime, new lead-time-in-days evaluation objective) versus the named STS-NET baseline, not a mere region re-application.
hard_constraint_verdict.H2: PASS - not any of the 8 banned patterns; explicitly positioned against, not as, a plain NDVI viewer.
hard_constraint_verdict.H3: PASS - Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical time series are the sole primary inputs; sensor, resolution, revisit, and licence are documented above.
hard_constraint_verdict.H4: PASS with caveat - EU arable farmers/insurers is the better-evidenced user segment given available ground-truth infrastructure; the Singapore/Malaysia framing is weaker and needs explicit justification or should be dropped in favour of EU.
hard_constraint_verdict.H5: PASS - small model architecture, small AOI dataset (15-30GB), all free-tier data and compute, comfortably under the 24GB/12h/RM200/200GB ceilings.
hard_constraint_verdict.H6: PASS - 'an alert that fires before NDVI moves, measured in days, beating what insurers use today' is a clear 60-second pitch with a concrete, live, dated demo.

overall_recommendation: VIABLE. The idea passes all six hard constraints and has a genuinely defensible novelty delta versus the named STS-NET baseline, but the single biggest open question - whether any real, non-circular ground-truth stress-event record can be obtained - remains unresolved after this search and must be the very first thing the student verifies, alongside an early empirical check of whether SAR actually adds lead time at all.
confidence: Medium. The arXiv/OpenAlex/Crossref/dblp searches and WebSearch dataset-access checks were thorough and internally consistent (STS-NET's abstract, the ASAP/Meroni baselines, and the Huo et al. counter-evidence all corroborate each other), but this pass did not directly query the Copernicus STAC catalogue for actual local revisit statistics on a specific candidate AOI, nor did it contact any EU national crop-monitoring body (e.g. a Sen4CAP partner) to confirm dated stress-event data availability. Confidence would rise materially with either of those two direct checks.
